A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerSyn research. All 19 pages in each version, including Appendix A.1–A.6, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning and mathematical-reasoning experiments, including benchmark results in Table 2 and additional experiments and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, router evaluations, and appendix experiments reported in v1.

M1.justification: The reward criterion, Bradley–Terry training objective, routing procedure, and student fine-tuning remain unchanged. Section 2.3 clarifies the router output and documents its linear head without reporting an alteration to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Magpie-Zoo and PerSyn-Math for training and evaluate on IFEval, TruthfulQA, LiveBench, GSM8K, MATH, and SVAMP. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Strong, Mix, Family-Strong, and CAR remain the benchmark comparators. The Oracle router comparisons and reward-model comparisons also retain their participants, including the baseline teacher assignments in Tables 11–12.

E3.justification: The dataset sizes, router training and evaluation splits, model configurations, metrics, decoding procedures, and training settings match. Appendix A.1 retains zero-shot evaluation except five-shot GSM8K; Tables 9–10 retain the same hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same reward ablations, alpha sensitivity study, router size and training-data analyses, teacher-allocation analyses, Long-CoT replacement experiment, and reward-model strength comparison. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen2.5-3B PerSyn scores of 44.16 on IFEval and 57.80 on MATH; the Oracle comparisons and plotted results also match.

T1.justification: The real-valued router output domain and Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Section 2.3 explains that the outputs are unnormalized logits and that their differences yield pairwise probabilities through a sigmoid, clarifying the existing formulation without adding mathematical results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about personalized teacher selection, efficient route-then-generate synthesis, performance across student families and scales, and the PerSyn-Math dataset.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning quality versus learnability, smaller teachers, and the selective usefulness of Long-CoT teachers remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning untested domains and student models larger than 14B.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 newly specifies that the Qwen2.5-1.5B router replaces its language-modeling head with a linear coefficient head whose output dimension equals the teacher count. This adds implementation information; the appendix hyperparameters, hardware, and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liang et al. (2026), Training LLMs for Divide-and-Conquer Reasoning Elevates Test-Time Scalability, to the introduction and references. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier distillation methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands Section 2.3 to explain router scores, pairwise probabilities, and the loss more clearly. It also adds an acknowledgement and makes small wording and reference-spacing edits, while retaining the overall section and appendix structure.

P2.justification: The existing displays shift with text reflow: Figure 2 moves from page 5 to 6, Figure 6 from page 7 to 8, and Table 3 changes column position. Table 1's caption is refined; no figure or table is added or redrawn.

improvement.justification: Section 2.3 reduces ambiguity about router scores and pairwise probabilities and supplies the previously unspecified linear output-head detail. These changes modestly improve clarity and reproducibility. The experimental evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
